problem: The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}-8{x}^{3}}{2{x}^{3}-5x}$ is $y=${{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

In this case, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{3}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}-8{x}^{3}}{2{x}^{3}-5x} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{8{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{5x}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{x}-8)}{(2-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{1}{x}$ and $\frac{5}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{1}{x}-8)}{(2-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & \to \frac{0-8}{2+0} \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-4.$
